industry_cases.onepager_lede: Cloudflare's problem arrived before its agents did. An organization accumulates more engineering standards than any one person can hold in their head, and every change risks quietly breaking one; Cloudflare's answer was to turn the standards themselves into durable, machine-readable knowledge, each requirement given a stable identity that survives the edits around it. Agents then enforce those standards at the moment of review, while people keep the authority to author and promote policy. The book reads the case as a bet that autonomy works once institutional knowledge is made legible to the machine, retrieved where the work happens, and enforced without its author present.

scale_facts: nearly a quarter of a million standards violations flagged
~16,000 resulting in withheld approval
~600 unique open specs reviewed (3,200+ invocations)
200+ incident reports assessed

industry_cases.autonomous_work: Agents review code/design/incident artifacts and may withhold approval or block a merge on an unsatisfied enforced MUST; humans author, approve, and promote policy. Agents scale reach, not authority.
industry_cases.traceability: Stable requirement slug survives RFC edits (identity, not location); statements retain pointers back to originating RFC sections. LLM interprets applicability at review time — NOT a mechanical model<->implementation drift join.
industry_cases.context_strategy: Lazy/on-demand retrieval of relevant statements per merge request; representation compacted from Markdown to filtered JSON so agents pull only what applies.
industry_cases.agent_authority: Merge-block / approval-withhold on enforced statements; no autonomous policy change; promotion approved->enforced is human-gated.
industry_cases.feedback_adaptation: Representation evolution is automated (RFC change -> re-extract/compact); POLICY evolution is human-governed. The incident agent surfaces gaps, and the source (source D, 'Code Orange: Fail Small is complete') DOES describe finding -> new obligation -> enforcement (incident -> RFC -> Codex rule -> agent review); what the source does NOT describe is the measured recurrence-retired / recurrence-drop that would close the loop.
industry_cases.org_memory: Codex = curated RFC corpus as durable institutional knowledge outliving any engineer or team.
industry_cases.implicit_theory: The book reads Cloudflare as appearing to believe autonomous agents work when institutional standards are made machine-readable, given stable identities, retrieved at the point of work, and enforced by agents at review time.

industry_cases.onepager_lede: Spotify is the case where the environment came first. For years before autonomous coding agents existed, Spotify had been standardizing its software estate for human engineers and deterministic bots: a catalog that named every service and its owners, fleet-wide tooling that could push a single change across thousands of repositories, and an automatic gate that admitted work on evidence. That long head start is both the case's defining feature and its evidential gift. The environment was mature and measured before the agent arrived, so Spotify offers something close to a before-and-after on what a governed substrate buys you, with the caution that the productivity figures are self-reported rather than a causal test.

source.author_role: engineering (internal-practice retrospective: Charas + Bruggmann + platform staff)

scale_facts: >1,500 merged AI-generated (Honk) PRs; hundreds of internal users (Nov 2025 - Apr 2026)
>300,000 automated changes merged by 2023 (~75% automerged); 2.5M+ cumulative automated maintenance PRs by 2026
60-90% estimated time savings for studied migrations (self-reported/observational, not a causal estimate; reported in the Honk Part 1 material, not Part 4)
Log4j patch reached ~80% of production backend services within 9 hours; framework adoption to 70% of fleet fell from ~200 days to <7 days
94% of engineers report higher productivity and a 76% increase in PR frequency (self-reported June 2026 survey - adoption/perceived value, not a causal effect)

industry_cases.autonomous_work: Honk inspects repos, edits code, builds/tests via per-repo verifiers, opens PRs, runs unattended across many repos (one Kubernetes pod per task), and by 2026 accepts work conversationally from Slack. Targeting is templated (Fleetshift selects repos); implementation is open-ended (the agent determines its own path). Admission is automated (automerger); humans own migration intent, standards, and ambiguous field mappings.
industry_cases.traceability: Partial. Component/dependency/endpoint-lineage models with stable component identities in Backstage; auto-generated architecture diagrams stay synced to metadata (drift-free by construction); Firewatch links each automerged PR to later deploy/pipeline failures. But no generalized deterministic drift gate that maintains model<->implementation parity over the code the agent edits and can block divergence.
industry_cases.context_strategy: Explicit reasoning-horizon management: the first home-grown loop overflowed on too-broad file selection and starved on too-narrow, and the agent forgot the task once context filled; the response was outcome-oriented prompts, one-change-at-a-time decomposition, deliberately restricted tools, upfront context condensation, and verifiers that parse large build/test output and return only a compact relevant result (the validator hides irrelevant mechanics as well as judging correctness). No context-reduction metric published.
industry_cases.agent_authority: High reasoning autonomy inside a deliberately narrowed action surface: a standardized restricted tool set, Git exposed only through a limited tool, allow-listed Bash, a per-task Kubernetes-pod container, Claude via the Agent SDK. The agent opens PRs but holds no merge authority - admission is a separate automated gate. Git authority, available commands, and whether an invalid change may advance are environmental, not prompt-level.
industry_cases.feedback_adaptation: Two loops. Loop A (concrete): observed agent-loop failures drove environmental changes - a CI fail led to an independent verifier abstraction + automatic pre-PR enforcement; scope creep led to an LLM judge that vetoes and requests correction (~25% veto rate, ~50% self-correct). Loop B (stated intent, not a measured loop): the Scio struggle diagnosed 'the ecosystem lacks standardization/tests', pushing standardized frameworks and a testing prerequisite - a change to the substrate itself, framed by Spotify as forward-looking strategy.
industry_cases.org_memory: The pre-agent platform - Fleet Management, Fleetshift, the Backstage catalog, the System Model, Soundcheck standards, the automerger, Firewatch, standardized stacks - was built for human engineers and deterministic bots years before Honk, then became the substrate for autonomous coding; the Chief Architect credits that earlier investment for Spotify's AI-readiness.
industry_cases.implicit_theory: The book reads Spotify as treating the software estate as one governable fleet: standardize it enough that changes are predictable, model its components/dependencies/ownership/standards, automate targeting/execution/admission/monitoring, give a probabilistic agent only the transformation problem deterministic automation handles poorly, constrain its tools, verify independently, and automatically admit on strong evidence - the platform, not the model alone, decides whether autonomy scales.

industry_cases.result_sentence: Spotify built a standardized, model-backed, automatically-governed engineering substrate for humans and deterministic bots over several years, then swapped the deterministic transformation function for a probabilistic reasoner when autonomous coding agents arrived and left the surrounding targeting, verification, admission, and monitoring machinery essentially unchanged - the sample's cleanest demonstration that the governed environment is conceptually prior to the agent.

industry_cases.onepager_lede: Meet Shopify through River, an agent you summon from a public Slack channel to read code, run tests, query the data warehouse, and open a pull request. River is public on purpose: a lesson learned in a private session helps no one else, so every session becomes a searchable artifact the company mines into skills and defaults. Underneath sits the deliberate part, a single work surface that centralizes context and reproducible execution, where each new agent is a profile over the shared substrate rather than a platform of its own. Shopify's distinctive habit is organizational rather than technical, keeping the work visible so one engineer's experience becomes everyone's, on a short evidence horizon with outcome numbers the company reports itself.

scale_facts: 59,918 River sessions across 5,170 Slack channels touching 7,000+ employees; 3,536 merged River-coauthored PRs in 30 days
~1 in 8 company-wide merged PRs coauthored by River; median session 19 min / 50 tool calls
Quick: >50,000 internal sites created by >50% of the company
Autoresearch applied across 40+ metrics (Shopify-reported deployment gains, not independently measured); Roast analyzed thousands of test files

industry_cases.autonomous_work: River is summoned from public Slack to do open-ended knowledge + implementation work over a durable session (read code, run tests, query the data warehouse, inspect production traces, open PRs, occasionally challenge a plan); multiplayer (a thread can attract another engineer and a new constraint without losing history); one profile among many planned. Humans merge.
industry_cases.traceability: Weak-to-partial. Nix is the executable exception - it makes the dependency graph explicit and reproducible (a real model<->environment join). The broader knowledge surface is not shown as mechanically synchronized with source/system state; no generalized model-node<->implementation drift gate. The durable append-only session gives provenance over agent work, not a representation<->territory join.
industry_cases.context_strategy: World centralizes formerly-distributed context; skills load on demand; profiles scope which skills/extensions apply; the durable session survives while harness + sandbox die and are recreated (persistent knowledge != persistent context-window contents); Roast replays from a step without rerunning prior model calls. No quantified context-reduction figure.
industry_cases.agent_authority: Reasoning autonomy inside environmentally-bounded execution: sandbox policy carried in profiles, the harness runs outside the sandbox, disposable sandboxes, Roast restricts file-writing/command execution through tool interfaces. Boundaries live outside the agent; merge stays human. [credentials-via-proxy UNVERIFIED in the fetch - re-verify for the prose wave]
industry_cases.feedback_adaptation: Multiple genuine loops, each a structural response rather than a better prompt: private agent learning has an organizational ceiling -> River is public-channel-only, and sessions become searchable artifacts mined into skills/prompts/defaults; free-roaming AI over millions of lines was unreliable -> Roast (declarative hybrid workflows); every team wanting a bespoke agent -> Aquifer profiles (agent = configuration over a shared substrate); Quick data-capability misuse -> rate limiting. Converted artifacts are often soft (skill/prompt/default), not hard validators.
industry_cases.org_memory: World accumulates code + knowledge + skills + conventions + intent + agent instructions; public River sessions become harvestable corporate artifacts; Aquifer makes each next agent cheaper - 'add a bundle, not a platform'. The case's signature contribution.
industry_cases.implicit_theory: The book reads Shopify as holding that autonomous agents become organizationally useful when the environment is made common, reproducible, observable, and shared: consolidate the work surface, encode institutional knowledge in files/skills loaded at task time, make execution reproducible, separate durable sessions from disposable reasoning/execution, bound work in sandbox policies, make each new agent a profile over a shared platform, keep work public so local experience becomes shared knowledge, and combine probabilistic reasoning with deterministic steps for repeatable processes.

industry_cases.onepager_lede: Docker began from a question about trust: how much freedom can you give an agent whose behavior you cannot fully predict? Its answer moved the boundary off the prompt and into the runtime, giving each agent a disposable microVM where the forbidden thing is simply absent (the home SSH directory is not in the agent's world, rather than a rule telling it not to look), so inside the box it can install, run, and modify freely. On that footing Docker ran a small team of role-specialized agents on CI, each free to investigate the unexpected, with an independent reviewer and a human standing between every pull request and the main branch. It is the youngest system in the set, so read it for its architecture and authority story rather than for long-run outcomes.
industry_cases.distinctive_starting_point: authority boundaries + autonomous fleet + evaluation loops

source.author_role: engineering (Staff SWE internal-practice account: de la Pena; supporting Docker product posts)

scale_facts: 7 autonomous roles on CI (cli-tester, performance-tester, upgrade-tester, software-engineer, project-manager, product-owner, /build-engineer) over 20 skills (13 foundational + 7 role)
cli-tester: 52+ scenarios across 14 tiers
worker/reviewer loop up to 5 iterations by default (worker = Opus; reviewer = Opus with 1M context evaluating the full diff)
proactive software-engineer: weekly architect-mode scan -> up to 5 findings -> 3 parallel runners -> 3 PRs
reactive agent-fix: first draft often within ~1 hour
~2-week build horizon; ~2-week run horizon at report (small-sample; no aggregate dataset)

industry_cases.autonomous_work: A 7-role CI fleet: exploratory CLI testing (52+ scenarios / 14 tiers), performance and upgrade testing, reactive bug-fix (agent-fix label -> PR ~1h), a proactive weekly quality scan (5 findings -> 3 parallel runners -> 3 PRs), issue triage/dedup, project-board maintenance, and release-note generation. Roles are open-ended (investigate the unexpected, not compare to a fixed output - Docker's stated reason for roles over scripts). Agents open PRs, file issues, and manage the board; agents do NOT merge.
industry_cases.traceability: Weak. Durable task state lives in the issue/branch/commits/summaries/reviewer-feedback, giving provenance across fresh-context iterations, but there is no representation<->territory join (no model-node<->implementation drift check). Stable identity lives in GitHub artifacts, not in a synced system model.
industry_cases.context_strategy: The Ralph loop's answer to long-running reasoning: each iteration spawns a fresh agent with a clean context window; durable state lives outside the model invocation (issue, repo/branch, commits, summaries, tests, reviewer feedback); the next fresh agent reconstructs progress from those artifacts. Skill composition bounds per-role context (cli-tester loads /build-engineer + project-manager, not all knowledge). No quantified context-reduction figure.
industry_cases.agent_authority: Two boundaries, both OUTSIDE the agent. Runtime: each agent runs in a dedicated microVM sandbox with its own filesystem/workspace, network boundary (allow/deny lists), and Docker daemon; only the project workspace is mounted, no host reach; inside the box the agent has broad freedom (install/run/modify/execute unattended). Admission: agents create PRs but do not merge; architecture, priority, scope, and merge stay human. The boundary lives in the state space, not in prompts ('~/.ssh is not in the agent's world', not 'don't touch ~/.ssh'); delegation to parallel runners does not widen authority. Docker's stated product philosophy (product posts, corroborated by internal adoption in the Fleet report): guardrails enforced outside the agent, a true bounding box, and inside it move fast - hard boundaries enable MORE autonomy.
industry_cases.feedback_adaptation: Genuine loops, each a structural response: a noisy exploratory sensor (every anomaly -> issue; humans stop listening) -> dedup + confirm-before-file via the project-manager, with every discovering skill calling it before filing; building the top role first exposed missing foundations -> encode foundational skills that later roles inherit; CI-only iteration is slow -> develop locally then promote unchanged to CI; self-evaluation is insufficient -> add a separate reviewer invocation (generation != evaluation); host execution is too permissive -> move authority into the microVM. No reconcile/retire (young system).
industry_cases.org_memory: The 13 foundational skills (including the /build-engineer foundation everything else stands on) encode project knowledge once, reused by roles; the Ralph loop encodes iteration once; the sandbox encodes execution safety once; the project-manager centralizes triage; local/CI portability lets one skill serve both modes. Compounding structure, but a ~2-week horizon gives no long-term-returns evidence.
industry_cases.implicit_theory: The book reads Docker as holding that autonomous agents are useful because they investigate and act without continuous permission, so preserve that autonomy rather than suppress it: put hard execution boundaries outside the reasoner, give each agent a bounded sandbox + explicit role + project knowledge + only role-appropriate tools, compose reusable skills over monolithic prompts, use an iterative worker/reviewer loop instead of expecting first-pass correctness, run roles in CI but keep architecture/priority/scope/merge human, and when the fleet gets noisy improve the reusable substrate rather than patching each output.

industry_cases.onepager_lede: Siemens inverts the brownfield. Where the software companies built an environment around an arriving agent, Siemens's agents arrive into an engineering culture that spent decades encoding intent, geometry, physics, requirements, and verification into executable models, with code as one downstream artifact those models generate rather than the source of truth. On its sharpest prototype an engineer states intent in plain words ('validate this part under 200 lb in the Y-direction') and the agent reads the CAD geometry, sets up the finite-element model, calls the solver, and returns a validated report. This is the case that never had to be persuaded engineering should run through models; the evidence is prototype-and-product rather than a long deployment, and it comes from the vendor's own writing.
industry_cases.distinctive_starting_point: model-first engineering; models already are the development surface

source.author_role: Siemens Software technical contributors (prototype + product + architecture-vision blogs)

scale_facts: ~3-5 million CAE practitioners worldwide and ~30-50 million designers/engineers who need simulation insight (a market-size estimate, not an agent-deployment count)
autonomous simulation loop from intent to validated FE answer runs in under 60 seconds (prototype embedded in Siemens Designcenter NX)
A3E coverage target: automating ~80% of standard engineering tasks is stated as already sufficient
Capital auto-generates production code (C/C++, Java, Ada) from UML models; validation via SIL, virtual ECUs, requirements + code coverage, and generated test vectors

industry_cases.autonomous_work: On the strongest prototype the user supplies high-level intent ('validate this part under 200 lb in the Y-direction') and the agent autonomously interprets CAD geometry to find load/support faces, selects materials, assigns boundary conditions, chooses discretization, configures the finite-element model, invokes a headless solver, interprets the result, and produces a validated report - a multi-step engineering plan, not a one-shot transformation. Across the dossier: FE setup+solve+report, BOM navigation/impact-analysis/governed-change, and model-driven code generation. Work originates from human intent; the agent chooses how, not whether or what. The BOM agent requires human-in-the-loop confirmation and acts within existing governance.
industry_cases.traceability: Strong and native. Capital connects software architecture to electrical/network models, links requirements through Polarion + Teamcenter, imports normalized SysML, and creates a traceable digital thread across software/networks/electrical/electronics; the BOM agent adds a product->variant/effectivity->change axis. Agents inherit relationships engineers already formalized rather than reconstructing them. Honest ceiling: the sources describe rich synchronization/propagation but not a generalized deterministic drift gate that blocks an agent's model<->implementation divergence.
industry_cases.context_strategy: Reasoning-horizon management by architecture: A3E decomposes into task-scoped specialist agents ('3D Simulation Setup Agent', 'PLM Interface Agent', etc.) intentionally scoped to reduce hallucination. The deeper move is that the model IS the compression - a finite-element model restricts reality to geometry/material/loads/supports/discretization/physics, so the agent reasons over a reduced representation rather than the full artifact. No context-reduction metric reported.
industry_cases.agent_authority: High semantic autonomy inside strong domain and workflow authority: the agent plans, reasons over incomplete information, calls tools, and adapts, but operates through specialized engineering tools and workflows, not arbitrary execution. The BOM agent's actions happen within existing governance, access controls, and change processes, with human-in-the-loop confirmation for consequential BOM updates. The action space comes from domain semantics (geometry/materials/loads/solver/result; configure-product/where-used/replace/ECN). Honest ceiling: file/network/credential/sandbox granularity is not documented at Docker's level.
industry_cases.feedback_adaptation: The weakest field. Engineering-loop feedback is rich - model updates propagate downstream, design changes trigger new analysis, the executable digital twin turns operational data into insight, agents adapt under incomplete information. But governance conversion in the MAGE sense (an agent's recurring mistake -> structural diagnosis -> a new persistent mechanism that governs future agents) is not evidenced in the public material: much feedback changes the design, little changes the governance of future agents.
industry_cases.org_memory: Decades of formalized, executable engineering structure - model libraries, product models, simulation capability, code-generation pipelines, requirements traceability, verification tooling, PLM semantics, digital-thread links - none of it built for generative agents, all of it inherited from mature non-AI engineering disciplines, becoming agent capital the moment an agent can operate it. The most extreme external instance of inherited engineering capital.
industry_cases.implicit_theory: The book reads Siemens as taking model-first engineering as native: the authoritative representation of a physical/functional system is a model (with code as one downstream artifact the model generates), autonomous agents should operate the existing engineering machinery at the abstraction level where engineers make decisions, deterministic analysis (solvers, SIL, virtual ECUs, verification) supplies evidence downstream of the agent's semantic choices, and human judgment retains engineering intent and consequential authority.

industry_cases.index_blurb: Its agents arrive into decades of executable engineering models, with source code just one downstream artifact those models generate.
industry_cases.result_sentence: Siemens is the sample's case where the governed artifact is not source code but decades of executable engineering models, a digital thread, deterministic solvers, and governed change workflows, and MAGE's structural half maps onto it with almost no contortion - the strongest external support for treating software as one instance of Model-Based Agentic Engineering - with one honest soft spot exactly where MAGE is most distinctive: adaptive governance / governance conversion is not evidenced.

industry_cases.onepager_lede: Zenseact carries MAGE past source code. Its agents do not write software; they do knowledge work across the company's own systems, reasoning over issue trackers, code review, CI, search, and even ERP to decide which tool and which piece of expertise a task needs. The platform, called ZAP, is federated: a central team owns the runtime, permissions, and context machinery, while each domain team ships an agent as little more than a directory holding a config file and a skill. The origin is telling: an earlier, open approach 'did not scale,' so Zenseact rebuilt the environment around the same commodity models, betting that capability lives partly in the environment, on a single company-authored source that reports no outcome numbers yet.
industry_cases.distinctive_starting_point: autonomous knowledge work over distributed engineering systems

scale_facts: measured context reduction of 67-98% for financial queries and 43-97% for engineering queries via progressive skill disclosure (context cost measured; the reasoning-quality half asserted, not measured)
skill frontmatter budget ~1.5-2 KB total across all active skills (always in the system prompt); skill bodies injected only when the deterministic TF-IDF router scores them relevant
integrations span JIRA, Gerrit, Zuul, GoCD, Elasticsearch, SAP (ERP), Confluence, SharePoint, and proprietary internal tools, built on AWS Bedrock
creating a domain agent requires only a directory under agents/ with two files (config.yaml + SKILL.md); no productivity/defect/before-after outcome data and no stated deployment duration

industry_cases.autonomous_work: ZAP agents are more than document-retrieval chatbots: they use tools to act over enterprise systems and compose multi-step activity dynamically - deciding what information a task needs, which skill/tool is relevant, which action to perform, and whether to delegate to a specialist agent. Work leans toward engineering + enterprise knowledge work (investigation, synthesis, tool-mediated action across issue-tracking, code review, CI/CD, search, and financial/ERP systems), not autonomous source-code authorship; the autonomy is in reasoning about and orchestrating heterogeneous work.
industry_cases.traceability: Weak-to-absent as a model<->territory join. Skills reference the systems they operate over and tool schemas bind to specific enterprise APIs, but there is no representation<->territory drift check. Stable identity lives in the enterprise systems' own artifacts (JIRA keys, Gerrit changes, SAP records), not in a synchronized model of the system. The one traceable link the platform maintains is the disclosure record - which skills the TF-IDF router selected or missed per query - which is what makes disclosure-misses measurable.
industry_cases.context_strategy: The platform treats context as a scarce resource: Level-1 frontmatter (~1.5-2 KB across all active skills) is always in the system prompt; Level-2 skill bodies are injected only when a deterministic TF-IDF cosine-similarity router scores them relevant to the query. Measured context reduction of 67-98% (financial) / 43-97% (engineering) - the set's strongest measured reasoning-horizon instance - though the without-lowering-quality half is asserted, not measured.
industry_cases.agent_authority: Authority is explicit, machine-readable, and placed in the environment. Three stacked surfaces: a per-tool, per-role permission table (auto_approve / confirm-via-SSE / deny), so decide-freely != act-freely and the environment sets the line; agent-to-agent delegation that is allow-listed in config and depth-limited (the delegation topology is itself an authority model); and sanctioned tool seams with bidirectional sanitization (arguments validated for injection patterns; tool output scrubbed of prompt-injection markers). Boundaries live outside the reasoner.
industry_cases.feedback_adaptation: One clean loop plus a bootstrap-by-failure origin. The disclosure-miss loop: a task runs, the right skill exists but the TF-IDF router fails to surface it, the miss is detected and recorded as telemetry, an automated improvement pipeline analyzes it, and the skill/disclosure mechanism is updated so future agents get better context - the failure is diagnosed structurally (the environment failed to present the right representation) and the repair targets the environment. Origin: the prior open-source approach 'did not scale' and 'measurable outcomes were lacking', and ZAP is the structural response (same commodity models, a better-engineered environment). Not-described: strengthen / reconcile / retire (the subtractive arm).
industry_cases.org_memory: Federated engineering capital: skills make expert knowledge durable outside individual people and sessions. The central platform owns generic capital (runtime, tool/skill loading, permissions, context management, delegation, monitoring); domain teams own domain capital (their agents/tools/skills/knowledge, maintained where the expertise resides - an agent is just a directory + config.yaml + SKILL.md). Shopify centralizes; Zenseact federates. The disclosure-miss loop is capital maintenance - keeping the representation-routing fit between the capital and the reasoner.
industry_cases.implicit_theory: The book reads Zenseact as holding that enterprise autonomy scales when the organization separates a common agent platform from domain-specific intelligence: teams encode expertise as reusable skills + deterministic tools; agents receive only task-relevant context rather than the whole enterprise per session; probabilistic models decide what knowledge/operation is needed, but consequential actions execute through structured tools under explicit permission policies; agent-to-agent delegation is bounded like tool access; and the platform is instrumented so context-disclosure and capability-selection failures become evidence for improving the shared environment.

industry_cases.mage_explains_implicit: MAGE compresses Zenseact's separately-named skills / tools / agents / progressive disclosure / permissions / delegation / sanitization / monitoring into one governed environment - skills as soft conditioning, the TF-IDF router as a sensor + reasoning-horizon mechanism (and a determinization of context selection), tool schemas as sanctioned seams, the permission table as authority allocation + a human gate, the delegation allow-list as a constraint on the agent topology, sanitization as a trust boundary, disclosure-miss telemetry as a sensor, the improvement pipeline as governance conversion, and the platform/domain split as an agent stack over federated engineering capital - and names the structural-diagnosis question Zenseact performs but never states.
industry_cases.index_blurb: Carries the same governance past source code into federated knowledge work — deterministic tools behind structured seams, permissions per role.
industry_cases.result_sentence: Zenseact built a federated internal agent platform - deterministic tools behind structured seams, a per-tool/per-role permission table, bounded delegation, and a deterministic TF-IDF disclosure router with measured 67-98% / 43-97% context reduction - over distributed engineering-and-enterprise knowledge work rather than source code, carrying MAGE's Alignment, reasoning-horizon, capital, and conversion machinery cleanly beyond code (the governance half of the MBAE widening, complementary to Siemens's modeling half), with the honest bound that its churn/defect outcome vocabulary strains on non-artifact-production work and no effectiveness outcomes are reported.

cross_case_patterns._note: The Ch-6 three-bucket cross-case convergence — one row per PATTERN (not per site), co-located with construct_universe so the maps_to_construct join is cheap (a construct rename breaks the convergence build, CCP2). Three buckets: `universal` (what every source establishes) + `generalizes` (independently discovered, MAGE generalizes; support VARIES) project as tables via render_convergence_md(bucket); `distinctive` (the eight consequences of the environment-as-object viewpoint) is DATA the model owns (the list + the hedge + the nearest_external) but is rendered as PROSE, not a table, because a distinctive-MAGE row is all-`no` externally and reads as advocacy. support values are the closed set {yes, partial, no}, projected ✓ / partial / — . CCP3 checks every support map carries exactly the roster id-set, so a roster add reddens patterns that forgot the new site.
cross_case_patterns.distinctive_headline: MAGE is a theory of the engineering ENVIRONMENT ITSELF as the object of engineering: everyone else engineers an agent, a runtime, a policy engine, or a model; MAGE engineers the governed environment in which commodity intelligence operates.
cross_case_patterns.distinctive_spine: The distinctive bucket is not a flat list of eight independent inventions. It has one organizing claim above all of them — choose the environment as the object of engineering — and the Model Zoo, the Alignment Principle, the governance census, the gap/orphan metrics, the determinization frontier, governance conversion, engineering capital, reconcile/retire, and the comparative mechanism grammar all fall out of that one choice. This environment-as-object claim sits ABOVE Engineering Capital and Governance Conversion, because industry is independently discovering parts of those two (they sit in the 'generalizes' bucket), whereas the environment-as-object move is the one none of the six sites makes.
cross_case_patterns.distinctive_hedge: None of the external cases we examined describes the following machinery in the generalized form MAGE does. Not 'nobody in industry has ever done this.'

patterns.statement: Autonomy needs a representation the model cannot safely rebuild each run.

patterns.statement: The sanctioned tool seam, not the prompt, is where authority is allocated.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: MAGE generalizes the sanctioned tool seam as the place authority is allocated, not the prompt.

patterns.statement: The environment, not the reasoner, sets the limit on what an agent may do.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: MAGE names authority-in-the-environment as an Alignment invariant across all six sites.

patterns.statement: Probabilistic reasoning on the ambiguous; deterministic machinery on the decidable residue.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: MAGE names determinization as the general move: spend commodity intelligence on ambiguity, deterministic machinery on what has ceased to be ambiguous.

patterns.mage_generalization_note: MAGE names shared infrastructure as the E(0) each new agent drops into.

patterns.mage_generalization_note: MAGE names independent validation as an Alignment mechanism — generation is not evaluation.

patterns.mage_generalization_note: MAGE names the structural-diagnosis reflex; Siemens shows less evidence of changing the governance of future agents (the guidance's own qualification, the card §10 gap). Cloudflare is partial: it makes obligations machine-checkable and re-extracts on RFC change, and source D ('Code Orange: Fail Small is complete') describes the incident->RFC->Codex-rule->enforcement loop near-verbatim — but no measured recurrence-drop closes it, so partial is the ratified reading grounded in that described-but-unmeasured loop. Shows the review-amortization frontier is unevenly crossed.

patterns.statement: Scoped specialist roles instead of one monolithic agent.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: MAGE generalizes scoped roles as an authority + reasoning-horizon device; Docker (7 roles), Siemens (scoped specialist agents), Zenseact (delegation graph) are the strong cases; Spotify/Shopify partial (subagents/profiles); Cloudflare none.

patterns.statement: Act through a model of the system, not raw code.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: Spotify (lineage->repo set) and Siemens (BOM/model-driven code-gen) are the two strong cases; Docker has no model layer (no); the rest partial.

patterns.statement: The strongest notion of model — a Model Zoo spanning logical / behavior / process / physical / scenario / invariant / lineage / traceability views.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: MAGE proposes the full multi-view model set as the object of engineering. Among software-first sites, not-seen; only Siemens shows the idea is not fanciful — it is normal in model-based engineering.

patterns.statement: Explicitly binds the model to the territory — general model<->implementation parity plus a mechanical drift check.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: MAGE names a blocking parity gate over agent edits. Siemens's digital thread synchronizes and propagates, but is NOT a blocking parity gate; no site reaches the generalized discipline.

patterns.statement: A common grammar for governance mechanisms — representation / constraint / sensor / validator / gate / feedback as cross-technology types.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: The explanatory compression each case's analysis performs FOR the sites, never stated BY them; no external case names the grammar.

patterns.statement: Governance conversion as a general engineering operation — classify the failure, then choose the durable mechanism from model|constraint|sensor|validator|gate|interface|architecture|no-mechanism.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: MAGE names the abstraction, not the instance. Cloudflare (incident->RFC->Codex-rule->enforcement) is one described instance of an environmental response — source D ('Code Orange: Fail Small is complete') describes the loop and the record's governance-conversion cell reads partial — but the source shows no measured recurrence-closing conversion loop, so the generalized operation (classify-the-failure, then choose the durable mechanism) is MAGE-only. Cloudflare discovered the loop; MAGE names and generalizes it.

patterns.statement: Governs the accumulated governance itself — strengthen / reconcile / retire.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: Every external site is in accumulation mode; the subtractive arm (reconcile/retire) is the counterweight to 'more controls forever' and is MAGE-only in the corpus.

patterns.statement: Explicitly theorizes engineering capital — the compounding feedback loop as a dynamic, not just an accumulation.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: Spotify and Shopify near-name it; the full dynamic theory is MAGE-only.

patterns.statement: Integrates Modeling and Alignment as the two irreducible moves — better models make more obligations deterministically enforceable.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: The connective tissue no software case articulates: the two principles as one architecture, each strengthening the other.

patterns.statement: Treats the environment itself as the object of engineering — THE SPINE (RH2), not a peer of the other seven; they are its consequences.
patterns.mage_generalization_note: The shift from agent to environment is more explicit in MAGE than in any source. Ask what is missing from the environment that every future agent will inherit — no site makes the environment the object of engineering.
